abstract.p: Emotion detection in text is particularly challenging for low-resource languages due to linguistic diversity and cultural nuances. To promote inclusivity, SemEval introduces a multilingual, multi-label emotion dataset spanning several low-resource languages. We analyze this dataset to examine cross-lingual emotion distribution and address the performance limitations of existing models, which often overfit to high-resource language patterns. We propose AfroEmo, a multilingual emotion classification model built on Afro-XLM-R. Our approach involves adaptive pre-training on domain-specific corpora, followed by fine-tuning on the shared task dataset. We evaluate our model using Macro-F1, Micro-F1, and other official metrics. AfroEmo achieves a Macro-F1 of 0.71 on Amharic and shows strong generalization to Hausa and Yoruba. We further conduct an ablation study and error analysis to assess the contributions of each model component.
